## Summary

I redesigned the owner identity key to the v2 spec and made duplicate detection flow entirely through it. All tests pass (`Tests run: 2, Failures: 0, Errors: 0`, `BUILD SUCCESS`).

### What changed

**New: `Soundex.java`** — American Soundex encoding of the last name (first letter + three digits, standard b/f/p/v→1 … r→6 mapping with the h/w collapse rule), a package-private helper alongside `ShaHex`/`Household`.

**`ShaHex.java`** — added `lowerHex(String)` returning the full 64-char lowercase SHA-256 hex.

**`OwnerIdentity.key(Owner)`** — now returns `SHA-256 hex over (normalizedTelephone + '|' + lowerEmail + '|' + soundex(lastName))`. The `householdId` is no longer part of the key. This is also what the API exposes as the `identityKey` field, so the response is now a 64-hex string (satisfies `coreIdentityKeyIsSha256Hex`).

**`CheckOwnerIdentityUnique`** — unchanged logic (it already keyed off `OwnerIdentity.key`), so it automatically becomes the *single* 409 check on the new key; the household-derived 409 no longer exists as a separate condition. Still skips soft-deleted owners, still bypassed by `sharesHousehold`, and the email-domain blocklist still runs earlier in the pipeline (400 before this 409).
